questions.question: If A can complete a work in 10 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days, in how many days can they complete the work together?
questions.questionHtml: If A can complete a work in 10 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days, in how many days can they complete the work together?
questions.solution: A's 1 day work = 1/10, B's 1 day work = 1/15. Together their 1 day work = 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6. So they can complete the work in 6 days.
questions.subject: quantitative-aptitude

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 6 days and B can do it in 8 days. With the help of C, they completed the work in 3 days. Find the time taken by C alone.
questions.questionHtml: A can do a piece of work in 6 days and B can do it in 8 days. With the help of C, they completed the work in 3 days. Find the time taken by C alone.
questions.solution: A's 1 day work = 1/6, B's 1 day work = 1/8. (A+B+C)'s 1 day work = 1/3. So C's 1 day work = 1/3 - (1/6 + 1/8) = 1/3 - 7/24 = 8/24 - 7/24 = 1/24. C alone can do the work in 24 days.
questions.subject: quantitative-aptitude

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B. If A can complete a work in 12 days, how long will B take to complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: A is twice as efficient as B. If A can complete a work in 12 days, how long will B take to complete the same work?
questions.solution: Since A is twice as efficient as B, B will take twice as much time as A. B's time = 2 × 12 = 24 days.
questions.subject: quantitative-aptitude

questions.question: 20 men can complete a work in 15 days. How many men are required to complete the same work in 10 days?
questions.questionHtml: 20 men can complete a work in 15 days. How many men are required to complete the same work in 10 days?
questions.solution: This is an inverse proportion problem. More men means less time. Required men = (20 × 15)/10 = 300/10 = 30 men.
questions.subject: quantitative-aptitude

questions.question: A can do a work in 10 days. B can do the same work in 15 days. They work together for 4 days, then A leaves. In how many more days will B complete the remaining work?
questions.questionHtml: A can do a work in 10 days. B can do the same work in 15 days. They work together for 4 days, then A leaves. In how many more days will B complete the remaining work?
questions.solution: A's 1 day work = 1/10, B's 1 day work = 1/15. Together's 1 day work = 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6. In 4 days they complete 4/6 = 2/3 work. Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3. B will complete 1/3 work in (1/3)/(1/15) = 5 days.
questions.subject: quantitative-aptitude
